input.strategy_title: Experiment comparison for training and pipeline runs
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Data scientists iterate across dozens of training and pipeline runs but have no
way to compare them inside the platform: parameters and metrics live in
per-run pages, so comparison happens in exported spreadsheets. Model promotion
decisions need side-by-side visibility into what changed between candidate
runs and how their metrics differ. (Requirements below were consolidated from
two customer councils; some overlap in wording was kept from the sources.)

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | Users can select two or more runs and view their parameters and metrics side by side in the Dashboard. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Registered model versions link back to the run that produced them, so a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | Provide a run "diff" view that highlights which parameters and metrics changed between two selected runs. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers the comparison workflow from both the runs list and the registry. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Model Registry
- Data Science Pipelines

## Out of Scope

- Automatic best-run selection or promotion
- Comparison across clusters or across projects

## Open Questions

None.

# Run comparison view for training and pipeline runs (side-by-side and diff)

## Description

Delivers an experiment comparison capability in the Dashboard: users select
two or more training or pipeline runs and view their parameters and metrics
side by side, and can switch to a diff presentation that highlights which
parameters and metrics changed between two selected runs. This replaces the
current workflow in which data scientists export run data to spreadsheets to
compare experiments.

## Scope

- Multi-selection of two or more runs (training runs and Data Science
  Pipelines runs) from the existing runs surfaces in the Dashboard.
- A comparison view presenting the parameters and metrics of every selected
  run side by side.
- A diff presentation within the comparison view that highlights parameters
  and metrics whose values differ between two selected runs.
- The comparison reads run parameters and metrics through the existing
  per-run data surfaces; no change to Data Science Pipelines is in scope.
  Correct rendering of pipeline-run data in the comparison is the
  keep-working validation for that passively affected component.
- Out of scope: automatic best-run selection or promotion, and comparison
  across clusters or across projects.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a list of runs, when the user selects two or more runs and opens the
  comparison, then the parameters and metrics of every selected run are
  displayed side by side.
- Given two runs selected in the comparison view, when the diff presentation
  is opened, then the parameters and metrics whose values differ between the
  two runs are highlighted.
- Given runs produced by Data Science Pipelines, when they are included in a
  comparison, then their parameters and metrics render correctly through the
  existing run data surfaces without changes to Data Science Pipelines
  (passive-component validation).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): users can select two or more runs and view their parameters and
  metrics side by side in the Dashboard — primary coverage.
- HLR-3 (P1): run "diff" view highlighting which parameters and metrics
  changed between two selected runs — consolidated with HLR-1: the diff view
  is a presentation mode of the same comparison surface over the same run
  data, so both requirements are covered by this single epic at the higher
  priority.

# Run lineage on registered model versions

## Description

Registered model versions record the run (training or pipeline run) that
produced them, so that a comparison can later be opened from the Model
Registry. The linkage is exposed through the Model Registry's metadata
surfaces, using its existing extension model for structured metadata on model
versions.

## Scope

- A registered model version carries a reference to the run that produced it,
  retrievable through the Model Registry REST API.
- The reference is supported for model versions produced by both training
  runs and Data Science Pipelines runs.
- The concrete linkage mechanism (for example the existing custom-properties
  extension point on model versions, or another supported mechanism) is an
  implementation decision for the Model Registry team; the acceptance
  criterion is the functional outcome, not the mechanism.
- Out of scope: automatic population of the reference by best-run selection
  or promotion tooling.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a model version registered from a run, when the model version is
  queried through the Model Registry REST API, then the producing run is
  identifiable from the model version's metadata.
- Given model versions produced by training runs and by pipeline runs, when
  they are queried, then the run reference is present and resolvable for both
  run kinds.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P1): registered model versions link back to the run that produced
  them — data side (the registry-side linkage; the Dashboard-side entry point
  is covered separately).

# Open run comparison from the Model Registry

## Description

From a registered model version's page in the registry UI (rendered by the
Dashboard), users can open the run comparison populated with the run linked
to that model version, completing the registry-side entry point for the
experiment comparison workflow.

## Scope

- An entry point on the model version view in the registry UI that opens the
  run comparison capability.
- The opened comparison is populated with the run referenced by the model
  version's run-lineage metadata.
- Graceful handling of model versions that carry no run reference.
- Out of scope: comparison across clusters or across projects.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a registered model version that carries a run reference, when the
  user opens the model version in the registry UI and invokes the comparison
  action, then the run comparison opens populated with the linked run.
- Given a model version with no run reference, when its version page is
  viewed, then the comparison entry point is absent or disabled without
  error.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P1): registered model versions link back to the run that produced
  them, so a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry — UI side (the
  Dashboard registry integration consuming the run-lineage data).

# Document the run comparison workflow

## Description

User documentation for the experiment comparison workflow, covering both
entry points: the runs list in the Dashboard and the Model Registry. Content
follows the Red Hat docs content process.

## Scope

Content outline:

- Comparing runs from the runs list: selecting two or more training or
  pipeline runs, reading the side-by-side parameters and metrics view, and
  using the diff view to see what changed between two runs.
- Comparing runs from the Model Registry: opening a comparison from a
  registered model version that links back to its producing run.
- Guidance on what is not supported (automatic best-run selection or
  promotion; comparison across clusters or across projects), so users are not
  left looking for out-of-scope behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Documentation covers the comparison workflow starting from the runs list,
  including multi-run selection, the side-by-side parameters and metrics
  view, and the diff view.
- Documentation covers the comparison workflow starting from the Model
  Registry, including opening a comparison from a registered model version.
- Documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented behavior of
  the comparison workflow.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): documentation covers the comparison workflow from both the
  runs list and the registry.
